audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 16, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Maximum audit for Samuel's grief and safety fear, sacrificial concealment, trembling elders, appearance/heart contrast, David's age and absence, private anointing, Spirit transfer, harmful-spirit theology, music relief, royal service, armor-bearing, and possible double-introduction traditions.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Samuel, How long will you grieve over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen among his sons a king for myself.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Bethlehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.

modern.text: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל עַד מָתַי֙ אַתָּה֙ מִתְאַבֵּ֣ל אֶל שָׁא֔וּל וַאֲנִ֣י מְאַסְתִּ֔יו מִמְּלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מַלֵּ֨א קַרְנְךָ֜ שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֵ֤ךְ אֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֙ אֶל יִשַׁ֣י בֵּֽית הַלַּחְמִ֔י כִּֽי רָאִ֧יתִי בְּבָנָ֛יו לִ֖י מֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Samuel said, How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me. YHWH said, Take a heifer in your hand and say, I have come to sacrifice to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me. And the LORD said, Take an heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the LORD.

modern.text: “How can I go?” Samuel asked. “Saul will hear of it and kill me!” The LORD answered, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֵ֣יךְ אֵלֵ֔ךְ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שָׁא֖וּל וַהֲרָגָ֑נִי וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה עֶגְלַ֤ת בָּקָר֙ תִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ לִזְבֹּ֥חַ לַֽיהוָ֖ה בָּֽאתִי

verses.restored: Call Jesse to sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do; you shall anoint for me whom I say to you.

familiar.text: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will shew thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.

modern.text: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.”

original.text: וְקָרָ֥אתָ לְיִשַׁ֖י בַּזָּ֑בַח וְאָֽנֹכִ֗י אוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶֽׁר תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וּמָשַׁחְתָּ֣ לִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר אֹמַ֖ר אֵלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Samuel did what YHWH spoke and came to Bethlehem. Elders of city trembled to meet him and said, Is your coming peace?

familiar.text: And Samuel did that which the LORD spake, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?

modern.text: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled and asked, “Do you come in peace?”

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם וַיֶּחֶרְד֞וּ זִקְנֵ֤י הָעִיר֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֹ֥ם בּוֹאֶֽךָ

verses.restored: He said, Peace. I have come to sacrifice to YHWH. Sanctify yourselves and come with me to sacrifice. He sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to sacrifice.

familiar.text: And he said, Peaceably: I am come to sacrifice unto the LORD: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.

modern.text: “In peace,” he replied. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁל֗וֹם לִזְבֹּ֤חַ לַֽיהוָה֙ בָּ֔אתִי הִֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וּבָאתֶ֥ם אִתִּ֖י בַּזָּ֑בַח וַיְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֶת יִשַׁי֙ וְאֶת בָּנָ֔יו וַיִּקְרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ם לַזָּֽבַח

verses.restored: It happened when they came that he saw Eliab and said, Surely before YHWH is his anointed.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the LORD’s anointed is before him.

modern.text: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֔ם וַיַּ֖רְא אֶת אֱלִיאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַ֛ךְ נֶ֥גֶד יְהוָ֖ה מְשִׁיחֽוֹ

verses.restored: YHWH said to Samuel, Do not look toward his appearance or height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for it is not as human sees: human sees according to eyes, but YHWH sees according to heart.

familiar.text: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

modern.text: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אַל תַּבֵּ֧ט אֶל מַרְאֵ֛הוּ וְאֶל גְּבֹ֥הַּ קוֹמָת֖וֹ כִּ֣י מְאַסְתִּ֑יהוּ כִּ֣י לֹ֗א אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִרְאֶה֙ הָאָדָ֔ם כִּ֤י הָֽאָדָם֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה לַעֵינַ֔יִם וַיהוָ֖ה יִרְאֶ֥ה לַלֵּבָֽב

verses.restored: Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. He said, This one also YHWH has not chosen.

familiar.text: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.

modern.text: Then Jesse called Abinadab and presented him to Samuel, who said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א יִשַׁי֙ אֶל אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר גַּם בָּזֶ֖ה לֹֽא בָחַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Jesse made Shammah pass, and he said, This one also YHWH has not chosen.

familiar.text: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.

modern.text: Next Jesse presented Shammah, but Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”

original.text: וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר יִשַׁ֖י שַׁמָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר גַּם בָּזֶ֖ה לֹא בָחַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, YHWH has not chosen these.

familiar.text: Again, Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, The LORD hath not chosen these.

modern.text: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel told him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”

original.text: וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר יִשַׁ֛י שִׁבְעַ֥ת בָּנָ֖יו לִפְנֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל יִשַׁ֔י לֹא בָחַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בָּאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: Samuel said to Jesse, Are all young men complete? He said, The youngest remains, and look, he is shepherding sheep. Samuel said to Jesse, Send and take him, for we will not sit until he comes here.

familiar.text: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither.

modern.text: And Samuel asked him, “Are these all the sons you have?” “There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.” “Send for him,” Samuel replied. “For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל אֶל יִשַׁי֮ הֲתַ֣מּוּ הַנְּעָרִים֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר ע֚וֹד שָׁאַ֣ר הַקָּטָ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֥ה רֹעֶ֖ה בַּצֹּ֑אן וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל אֶל יִשַׁי֙ שִׁלְחָ֣ה וְקָחֶ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹא נָסֹ֖ב עַד בֹּא֥וֹ פֹֽה

verses.restored: He sent and brought him. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and good appearance. YHWH said, Arise, anoint him, for this is he.

familiar.text: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.

modern.text: So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח וַיְבִיאֵ֨הוּ֙ וְה֣וּא אַדְמוֹנִ֔י עִם יְפֵ֥ה עֵינַ֖יִם וְט֣וֹב רֹ֑אִי וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה ק֥וּם מְשָׁחֵ֖הוּ כִּֽי זֶ֥ה הֽוּא

verses.restored: Samuel took horn of oil and anointed him in midst of his brothers. Spirit of YHWH rushed upon David from that day onward. Samuel arose and went to Ramah.

familiar.text: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.

modern.text: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah. David Serves Saul

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶת קֶ֣רֶן הַשֶּׁ֗מֶן וַיִּמְשַׁ֣ח אֹתוֹ֮ בְּקֶ֣רֶב אֶחָיו֒ וַתִּצְלַ֤ח רֽוּחַ יְהוָה֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיָּ֣קָם שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הָרָמָֽתָה

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH turned aside from Saul, and a harmful spirit from YHWH terrified him.

familiar.text: But the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him.

modern.text: After the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him.

original.text: וְר֧וּחַ יְהוָ֛ה סָ֖רָה מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֑וּל וּבִֽעֲתַ֥תּוּ רֽוּחַ רָעָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Saul's servants said to him, Look, please, a harmful spirit of Divine is terrifying you.

familiar.text: And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.

modern.text: Saul’s servants said to him, “Surely a spirit of distress from God is tormenting you.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי שָׁא֖וּל אֵלָ֑יו הִנֵּה נָ֧א רֽוּחַ אֱלֹהִ֛ים רָעָ֖ה מְבַעִתֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Let our lord command your servants before you to seek a man who knows how to play lyre. When harmful spirit of Divine is upon you, he will play with his hand, and it will be well for you.

familiar.text: Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.

modern.text: Let our lord command your servants here to seek out someone who can skillfully play the harp. Whenever the spirit of distress from God is upon you, he is to play it, and you will be well.”

original.text: יֹאמַר נָ֤א אֲדֹנֵ֨נוּ֙ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ יְבַקְשׁ֕וּ אִ֕ישׁ יֹדֵ֖עַ מְנַגֵּ֣ן בַּכִּנּ֑וֹר וְהָיָ֗ה בִּֽהְי֨וֹת עָלֶ֤יךָ רֽוּחַ אֱלֹהִים֙ רָעָ֔ה וְנִגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ וְט֥וֹב לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Saul said to his servants, See, please, for me a man who plays well, and bring him to me.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.

modern.text: And Saul commanded his servants, “Find me someone who plays well, and bring him to me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שָׁא֖וּל אֶל עֲבָדָ֑יו רְאוּ נָ֣א לִ֗י אִ֚ישׁ מֵיטִ֣יב לְנַגֵּ֔ן וַהֲבִיאוֹתֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי

verses.restored: One of young men answered and said, Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows playing, a mighty man of strength, a man of war, discerning in speech, a man of form, and YHWH is with him.

familiar.text: Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, that is cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the LORD is with him.

modern.text: One of the servants answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. He is a mighty man of valor, a warrior, eloquent and handsome, and the LORD is with him.”

original.text: וַיַּעַן֩ אֶחָ֨ד מֵהַנְּעָרִ֜ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה רָאִ֜יתִי בֵּ֣ן לְיִשַׁי֮ בֵּ֣ית הַלַּחְמִי֒ יֹדֵ֣עַ נַ֠גֵּן וְגִבּ֨וֹר חַ֜יִל וְאִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֛ה וּנְב֥וֹן דָּבָ֖ר וְאִ֣ישׁ תֹּ֑אַר וַיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, Send to me David your son who is with sheep.

familiar.text: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, which is with the sheep.

modern.text: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח שָׁא֛וּל מַלְאָכִ֖ים אֶל יִשָׁ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁלְחָ֥ה אֵלַ֛י אֶת דָּוִ֥ד בִּנְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּצֹּֽאן

verses.restored: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them by hand of David his son to Saul.

familiar.text: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son unto Saul.

modern.text: And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them to Saul with his son David.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח יִשַׁ֜י חֲמ֥וֹר לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְנֹ֣אד יַ֔יִן וּגְדִ֥י עִזִּ֖ים אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח בְּיַד דָּוִ֥ד בְּנ֖וֹ אֶל שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: David came to Saul and stood before him. Saul loved him greatly, and he became bearer of his armor.

familiar.text: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.

modern.text: When David came to Saul and entered his service, Saul admired him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֶּאֱהָבֵ֣הֽוּ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיְהִי ל֖וֹ נֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלִֽים

verses.restored: Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David stand before me, please, for he has found favor in my eyes.

familiar.text: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favour in my sight.

modern.text: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David remain in my service, for I am pleased with him.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שָׁא֔וּל אֶל יִשַׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר יַעֲמָד נָ֤א דָוִד֙ לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָ֥צָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָֽי

verses.restored: It happened whenever spirit of Divine was upon Saul, David took lyre and played with his hand. Saul had relief, it was well for him, and harmful spirit turned aside from upon him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

modern.text: And whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would pick up his harp and play, and Saul would become well, and the spirit of distress would depart from him.

original.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בִּֽהְי֤וֹת רֽוּחַ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל וְלָקַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת הַכִּנּ֖וֹר וְנִגֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְרָוַ֤ח לְשָׁאוּל֙ וְט֣וֹב ל֔וֹ וְסָ֥רָה מֵעָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ הָרָעָֽה

translation_notes: Samuel's grief is not condemned as weakness; the question redirects him while acknowledging a real rupture.
Samuel fears Saul will kill him. Prophets and officials are not protected from political violence, and prudent safety planning is not faithlessness.
The sacrificial explanation functions as concealment within danger and requires ethical audit; it is not a general license for deception.
Bethlehem's elders tremble at Samuel's arrival, showing how religious authority can generate fear even without stated threat.
Verse 7 rejects appearance and height as reliable leadership measures, though verse 12 still describes David attractively; the narrative tension should remain.
David is the youngest and initially absent because he is working. Birth order and invisibility do not determine worth.
Private anointing does not authorize a child or young person to seize power, enter war, or accept unsafe adult expectations.
'Harmful spirit from YHWH' is ancient theological language. It must never diagnose mental illness, epilepsy, trauma, neurodivergence, or emotional distress as demonic, sinful, or Divine rejection.
Saul's distress is real and terrifying. He remains a person deserving care, privacy, and protection from stigma.
Music provides relief in the story but is not a substitute for professional medical or mental-health care when such care is needed.
David enters Saul's service through royal request to Jesse within a hierarchy. Favor and affection do not erase power imbalance or establish unrestricted consent.
Armor-bearing can expose a young servant to military danger; this role must not romanticize child soldiers.
The chapter's two introductions of David may reflect distinct traditions and require source-compositional audit.
safety_note: Do not use harmful-spirit language to stigmatize mental illness, trauma, disability, neurodivergence, seizures, or emotional distress. Do not tell people music alone replaces healthcare. Do not romanticize secret anointing, child soldiers, political deception, or a ruler's control over a young worker. Saul deserves humane care even after rejection.
